policy.purpose: Deterministic prompt planning and review guidance for the local H3 workflow.

t2va.timeline_goal: Describe the complete audiovisual progression from text.

i2va.timeline_goal: Begin exactly from the supplied first frame and develop forward.

fl2va.timeline_goal: Describe an observable continuous path from the first frame to the last frame.

l2va.timeline_goal: Infer a plausible opening and converge exactly to the supplied last frame.

ref2va.timeline_goal: State what each reference controls and preserve stable reference labels.

rules.requirement: Render structural prompt sections in English while preserving dialogue, lyrics, and visible text in their requested language.
Use explicit time ranges whose total matches the requested duration and describe visible intermediate changes rather than only start and end states.
Assign every reference a stable label and state whether it controls identity, appearance, product, style, motion, camera, or sound.
Separate diegetic action and ambience from non-diegetic music.
Express concrete continuity constraints in the positive plan; do not inject a generic negative-prompt template into an unsupported field.
Use one dominant camera movement per generated segment and specify its direction, amplitude, and speed.
Keep each H3 segment centered on one continuous, observable action even when the overall plan contains multiple shots.
Reuse the same canonical wording for recurring people, wardrobe, props, environment, lighting, and materials.
Every framing or camera change must support a stated narrative or product-display purpose.

approval_requirements: Both boundary assets exist before FL2VA execution.
Each boundary asset has an immutable asset identifier and SHA-256.
The customer-approved prompt version names the exact boundary asset versions.

allowed_when: Every adjacent segment shares the same approved boundary asset.
Identity, wardrobe, props, environment, lighting, and camera constraints are global.
A continuous audio plan exists independently of segment generation.
disallowed_when: Dialogue or lip movement crosses a boundary.
A continuous camera move crosses a boundary.
Fast action, object handoff, or complex physical motion crosses a boundary.
Precise musical timing spans multiple segments.

stitching_rules: Use the same boundary image as the previous segment's last frame and the next segment's first frame.
Remove the duplicate first boundary frame from every segment after the first.
Keep frame rate, color characteristics, dimensions, and encoding settings consistent.
Report measured duration instead of assuming the requested nominal duration.
audio_rules: Prefer one continuous source or final track for the complete composition.
Do not treat independently generated segment audio as a continuous dialogue track.
Only use short normalized crossfades for non-dialogue ambience when no continuous source exists.

global_rules: Do not invent price, efficacy, certification, availability, brand ownership, or legal claims.
Keep supplied product geometry, material, labeling, and visible text stable.
End advertising-oriented videos with a deliberate product or brand state instead of an accidental final frame.

ecommerce: Describe product structure, material, demonstration action, use context, and verified benefit as separate fields.
social_commerce: Use the sequence problem, use process, observable benefit, and call to action without unsupported claims.
seeding: Favor credible first-person discovery, concrete use details, and an honest recommendation tone.
tvc: Give every shot a brand-building purpose and reserve a stable closing beat for the product or mark.
ai_ad: Establish the subject quickly, create one memorable visual transformation, and finish with clear brand information.
short_drama: Lock character, wardrobe, location, and visual style before generation; keep one continuous dramatic action per segment.
dynamic_comic: Lock character sheets, art style, panel composition, and shot plan before animating individual segments.

rules.requirement: Bind every review to the exact output identifier, prompt version, input hashes, and output SHA-256.
Translate each issue into a time range, severity, affected prompt field, and minimal revision; leave unrelated fields unchanged.
A model verdict may recommend approval or regeneration but never approves a customer stage.
Generate a revised prompt suggestion without submitting a new generation task until the customer explicitly requests regeneration.
Only customer-approved successful outputs may become reusable examples or preference data.
